key_insight: A history kernel indexed by time lag and Reynolds number captures sphere-flow memory beyond creeping flow, including non-monotonic responses at higher Reynolds numbers.
engineering_relevance: The kernel can improve transient hydrodynamic-force predictions for spheres when finite-Reynolds-number fluid memory matters.
method: Extract kernels from axisymmetric Navier–Stokes simulations of finite acceleration and deceleration ramps.
Cover initial Reynolds numbers from 0.2 to 200 while recovering the short-lag and creeping-flow Basset limits.
Extend beyond resolved time lags using far-wake asymptotics.
evidence_signal: For tested ramps, oscillatory forcing and non-periodic composite velocity histories, the kernel substantially improved history-force predictions over the literature formulations considered without case-specific adjustment.
watch_item: Validation is limited to the tested fixed-sphere, spatially uniform, axisymmetric flow conditions; broader applicability requires further evaluation.
paper_title: Fluid memory beyond creeping flow: a history kernel for a sphere at finite Reynolds numbers
